title: Reproductive system, floral biology and pollinators of Abutilon grandifolium in urban green spaces of Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires.
decision_basis: Primary study records legitimate versus illegitimate visits and visitor identities across two urban sites but does not test an independently measured floral or visitor-flower access geometry predictor against robbery route use.
notes: Route-resolved visitor behavior without the focal geometry predictor.

title: Hawaiian Endemic Honeycreepers (Drepanidinae) are Nectar Robbers of the Invasive Banana Poka (Passiflora tarminiana, Passifloraceae)
decision_basis: Study documents that two honeycreeper species robbed all banana-poka flowers they visited and interprets the 60–90 mm corolla tube as the mechanical cause, but there is no quantitative variation/comparison of geometry against route probability or frequency.
notes: Strong mechanistic natural-history evidence, but not a formal geometry-response estimate.

title: Reproductive biology and flower-visitor interactions of two bromeliad species from the Brazilian Atlantic Forest
decision_basis: Primary study characterizes reproductive biology, floral visitors and interaction modes in two bromeliads but does not estimate access geometry as a predictor of robbery route use.
notes: Flower-visitor natural-history comparison outside the direct geometry-to-route estimand.

title: What are the plant reproductive consequences of losing a nectar robber?
decision_basis: Primary study experimentally quantifies reproductive consequences of nectar robbing and temporal loss of a robber; robbery is the exposure whose plant-fitness consequences are estimated, not an outcome predicted by access geometry.

title: Bumblebees with big teeth: revising the subgenus Alpigenobombus with the good, the bad and the ugly of numts (Hymenoptera: Apidae)
decision_basis: Taxonomic/phylogenetic revision notes enlarged toothed mandibles and nectar robbing in long-corolla flowers but does not estimate a geometry-to-robbery route relation across biological units.
notes: Morphological adaptation context, not an ecological direct-test program.

title: Ecological Roles of Indian Palm Squirrels ( spp.) as Floral Funambulus Visitors Across Five Indian States: First Comprehensive Account
decision_basis: Study classifies opportunistic squirrel flower visits as nectar robbery, predation or occasional visitation across documented events but does not test access geometry as the predictor of route category.
notes: Functional natural-history inventory without focal geometry predictor.

title: Reproductive ecology of the aromatic plant Agastache mexicana (Lamiaceae): A valuable species to be used in urban pollinator gardens
decision_basis: Study records pollinators, nectar robbers and other visitors; modeled predictors of visitor activity include ambient temperature and co-flowering context rather than floral access geometry.
notes: Ecological-context predictor, outside the geometry-to-route contract.

title: Does competition for pollinators contribute to structuring Erica communities?
decision_basis: Field experiment relates pollination and nectar-robbing rates to resident Erica floral density/community context; floral density is the predictor, not visitor-flower access geometry.
notes: Community competition study with route outcome but non-geometric predictor.

title: Implicaciones ecológicas y evolutivas del robo de néctar en ecosistemas neotropicales venezolanos
decision_basis: Record is a doctoral thesis/dissertation-level synthesis rather than the primary peer-reviewed study report used as the formal bibliographic unit; component empirical papers must enter separately if eligible.
notes: Do not count an umbrella dissertation as an independent study program in addition to its component sources.

title: Geographic isolation, pollination syndromes, and pollinator generalization in HimalayanRoscoeaspp. (Zingiberaceae)
decision_basis: Study quantifies pollinator importance and identifies butterflies/moths as nectar robbers while describing floral–visitor mismatch, but does not estimate a quantitative geometry/mismatch predictor against robbery probability or frequency.
notes: Pollination-syndrome and visitor-role study, not formal geometry-to-route response model.

title: Nectar Robbing by the Purple-rumped Sunbird Nectarinia zeylonica from Introduced Flowers in Sri Lanka.
decision_basis: Short natural-history report documents nectar robbing by a sunbird on introduced flowers but provides no quantitative access-geometry predictor versus robbery response.
notes: Robbery occurrence record without geometry-response estimate.

title: Effects of nectar robbing on nectar dynamics and bumblebee foraging strategies in Linaria vulgaris (Scrophulariaceae)
decision_basis: Primary field study explicitly compares bumblebee proboscis length with legitimate versus secondary-robbing tactics; shorter-tongued bees were more likely to switch to secondary robbing whereas longer-tongued bees were less likely to switch.
notes: Eligibility frozen before direction coding; visitor–flower access morphology is the focal predictor and route choice is directly observed.

title: Optimizing size thresholds in a plant–pollinator interaction web: towards a mechanistic understanding of ecological networks
decision_basis: Study models plant–pollinator interaction occurrence using proboscis length and nectar-holder dimensions; it does not model legitimate versus robbery/bypass route use.
notes: Mechanical trait-matching network study without robbery-route response.

title: Variation in sexual size dimorphism and fit to Rensch's rule in Costa Rican hummingbirds
decision_basis: Study tests Rensch's rule and sexual size dimorphism in hummingbirds; no floral robbery route outcome is analyzed.
notes: Search false positive from hummingbird morphology context.
